title: PHACTn enables training-free, context-independent inference of nucleotide variant tolerance across the genome
summary: Accurate prediction of single-nucleotide variant (SNV) tolerability across the entire human genome remains a fundamental challenge in computational genomics, particularly for non-coding regions where the regulatory landscape is vast and poorly understood. Machine learning classifiers suffer from data circularity and demographic bias, while genomic language models demand massive computational resources and offer little biological interpretability. Here, we present PHACTn (Phylogeny-Aware Computing of Tolerance for nucleotide variants), a training-free, parameter-minimal method that infers nucleotide variant tolerability by traversing the mammalian phylogenetic tree and explicitly modeling the evolutionary independence of observed substitutions and their distance from the query species. With only 4 interpretable parameters, no training and no GPU requirement, PHACTn outperforms all evaluated tools on non-coding variants curated from both the ClinVar, and on non-coding variants potentially responsible for selected Mendelian diseases curated from OMIM. Additionally, it achieves state-of-the-art performance on variants within the informative range of alignment-based inference. These results establish that principled probabilistic phylogenetic modeling captures evolutionary constraint signals that large-scale sequence models fail to recover, offering a powerful, accessible, and mechanistically transparent alternative for genome-wide variant effect prediction.

title: Janusein and EB Cooperate to Enhance Microtubule Plus-end Catastrophe
summary: Microtubule (MT) plus ends are organized by end-binding (EB) proteins, yet how EB-associated factors modulate the transition from growth to catastrophe remains incompletely understood. Using spatially resolved proximity proteomics, we identified Janusein (ZC2HC1A) as a conserved, poorly characterized MT-associated protein (MAP). At low expression levels, Janusein tracked MT plus ends and reduced EB comet velocity; at higher levels, it redistributed to the MT lattice and was associated with MT bundling and widespread MT loss. Loss of Janusein resulted in spindle defects in human cells. In vitro, Janusein alone facilitated MT elongation through its C-terminal fragment, but promoted MT catastrophe through its N-terminal fragment in the presence of EB proteins. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses suggest that an N-terminal loop may perturb lateral contacts between adjacent MT protofilaments. Together, these findings identify Janusein as an unconventional MAP that functionally cooperates with EB proteins to promote MT catastrophe.

title: Community needs for FAIR pathogen data: a cross-sectional survey of infectious-disease researchers and educators
summary: Background: Datasets related to infectious diseases are essential for public health decision-making, yet their reuse remains limited by persistent barriers to data sharing and integration. Achieving data that are Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) is widely recognized as essential for accelerating scientific discovery and enabling coordinated responses to emerging threats, but the needs of the global pathogen data community have not been systematically characterized. Aim: This study, conducted by the Pathogen Data Network (PDN), aims to identify infrastructural and educational priorities among stakeholders working with infectious disease-related data, namely researchers, educators, healthcare professionals, bioinformaticians, and policymakers who generate, curate, or use pathogen data, in order to guide community-responsive support for data sharing and interoperability. Methods: A cross-sectional stakeholder survey was disseminated as an open, non-probability (convenience) survey to prospective participants reached through PDN networks, targeted mailing lists, and open professional and social-media channels. A total of 136 responses from researchers, healthcare professionals, bioinformaticians, and educators were analyzed descriptively to identify prioritized barriers, training needs, and preferred support mechanisms. Results: Respondents consistently identified structural constraints as the primary impediments to effective data use, including limited funding (74%), data-aggregation challenges (68%), and a shortage of skilled personnel (52%). Respondents identified bioinformatics for infectious disease research (68%) as the highest priority for training, followed by guidance on using the integrated pathogen data and tools portal provided by the PDN, the Pathogens Portal (51%). The Pathogens Portal was also ranked as the most essential PDN resource (72%). Preferred training formats included virtual short courses (68%) and webinars (66%). Notably, while researchers emphasized technical subjects like machine learning, educators prioritized foundational case studies. Conclusion: These findings provide an evidence-based descriptive summary of community needs and suggest that barriers to FAIR pathogen data are predominantly systemic rather than purely technological. The survey framework and openly available dataset offer a reusable template for assessing needs in other communities and regions. By aligning training, infrastructure development, and outreach with empirically identified priorities, organizations supporting infectious disease research can strengthen the interoperability and reuse of data and establish a benchmark for future community-driven improvements.

title: Domain Adaptation Improves Cross-site Classification of First-episode Schizophrenia from Multimodal Neuroimaging Data
summary: Identifying robust neuroimaging markers associated with schizophrenia is essential for advancing research and informing clinical understanding. However, a major obstacle to clinical translation is the limited ability of neuroimaging-based classification models to generalize across scanning sites. In this study, we first establish best performing within-site models, and then systematically investigate cross-site generalization in first-episode schizophrenia (FES) classification and evaluate strategies for mitigating site-related distribution shifts. Using data from two acquisition sites (n=544), we examine ComBat, CovBat, optimal transport, and deep adaptation. Across functional, structural, and diffusion-based features, both traditional machine learning (TML) and neural network (NN) models achieved comparable performance in within-site classification, with resting state fMRI functional connectivity providing the most robust unimodal features. When models are transferred across sites, performance degraded substantially across all approaches, by 5 to 12 percentage points of balanced accuracy. Distribution-alignment methods partially mitigated this degradation. Harmonization recovered 6 to 8 points for functional connectivity in one transfer direction, mainly by correcting a displaced decision threshold. Deep adaptation recovered similar gains but less consistently. Increasing model complexity alone did not result in systematic performance gains. Across the classifiers tested on this pair of sites, multimodal feature fusion did not consistently outperform functional connectivity alone. Overall, our findings indicate that controlling for site effects was more critical than model complexity for achieving generalizable classification in FES. These results come from two sites of a single coordinated study, and whether they hold for more heterogeneous sites remains to be tested.

title: Screening and evaluation of medicine food homology herbal combinations for ameliorating chemotherapy induced ovarian aging under an integrated multi-strategy framework
summary: Abstract Background: Ovarian aging poses a serious threat to women's reproductive health. Medicine food homology (MFH) herbs, owing to their favorable safety profile and suitability for long-term use, have become important interventional resources. However, conventional formula screening relies largely on empirical statistics and lacks mechanistic evidence and a systematic screening strategy. Methods: In this study, we integrated single cell transcriptomic analysis, human use evidence mining, UPLC/Q TOF MS chemical profiling and pretrained protein molecular representation models to establish a multi strategy framework for the discovery of MFH herbal combinations. Single cell transcriptomic datasets related to ovarian aging from the GEO database were analyzed to identify key pathological processes and candidate targets. High-frequency MFH herbs were selected by mining classical prescriptions and clinical literature. By comparing six protein molecular pretrained representation combinations, ESM T5 was identified for compound target affinity prediction and validated by molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, ultimately identifying the Astragalus ginseng (Huangqi Renshen) herb pair (HXF) as the core candidate. Functional expression validation of key targets was performed, and the efficacy of HXF and the expression of related molecules were verified in a D gal induced KGN granulosa cell senescence model and a cyclophosphamide-induced rat model of diminished ovarian function. Results: Single cell analysis revealed that ovarian aging was characterized by impaired steroidogenesis, enhanced MDK NCL communication between granulosa cells and immune cells, and extracellular matrix remodeling, with CYP19A1, SERPINE1 and MDK as key targets. By further integrating human-use evidence mining and UPLC/Q TOF MS compound annotation, an MFH compound library comprising 712 molecules was established. ESM T5 prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and SPR assays confirmed that multiple constituents of Astragalus and ginseng exhibited favorable binding activity toward key targets. At the cellular level, knockdown of MDK or SERPINE1 attenuated the senescence phenotype, whereas knockdown of CYP19A1 aggravated it. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that Astragalus ginseng ameliorated granulosa cell senescence and diminished ovarian function in rats, restored CYP19A1 related steroidogenesis, downregulated inflammation- and matrix remodeling related molecules such as SERPINE1 and IL18, and reduced MDK NCL colocalization signals. Conclusion: This study established a multi-strategy screening framework integrating disease mechanism decoding, human use evidence constraints and pretrained model prediction, and identified Astragalus ginseng as a candidate herb pair for ameliorating ovarian aging. Its effects may be associated with promoting steroidogenesis, suppressing SERPINE1/IL18 related inflammation and matrix remodeling, and modulating MDK NCL signaling. These findings provide a strategic reference for the mechanism oriented discovery of MFH herbal combinations.

title: Cross-family learning transfers thermal adaptation between enzymes
summary: Thermal adaptation has evolved independently across diverse protein families, yet whether the information underlying this adaptation can be transferred between evolutionarily unrelated proteins remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that thermostability can be learned from divergent protein families and transferred to enzymes without relying on their evolutionary ancestry. We developed THOR (THermally Optimised Representations), a generative framework that learns background-specific sequence transformations between unpaired mesophilic and thermophilic sequence populations while preserving the identity of the starting protein. Across evolutionarily divergent enzyme families, THOR transferred thermostability without exposure to thermophilic homologues during training. In malate dehydrogenase, excluded from cross-family training, zero-shot designs increased apparent melting temperature by up to 15 , with gains reaching 36  following limited family-specific fine-tuning. Majority of designed variants retained activity following prolonged thermal challenge, while selected variants exhibited nearly threefold higher catalytic turnover than wild type. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that comparable thermal phenotypes emerge through distinct, background-dependent changes in protein flexibility and stabilising interactions. Together, these findings demonstrate that thermal adaptation encodes transferable information beyond lineage-specific evolutionary solutions, revealing evolution as a source of reusable adaptive principles for engineering phenotypes in proteins whose evolutionary lineages have never acquired them.

title: Site Specific Hydration Contributes to the Thermal Stability of Proteins and Protein-Complexes
summary: Water is integral to protein structure and stability, yet ensemble measurements rarely identify the hydration interactions associated with stabilization. Here, variable-temperature electrospray ionization ion mobility mass spectrometry, conformation-resolved thermodynamic analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations are combined to examine solvent-dependent thermal stability of chymotrypsin inhibitor 2 (CI-2), a model two-state folder, and the barnase-barstar (Bn-B*) complex, which contains a highly polar binding interface. Replacing H2O with D2O raises the thermal transition temperature of both systems by approximately 3 {degrees}C, favors compact conformations, and reduces the relative thermodynamic accessibility of extended states. The conformationally resolved enthalpy-entropy compensation reveals D2O increases enthalpy for CI-2 but reduces enthalpy for Bn-B* as a result of opposing effects on the individual subunits of the complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that lower solvent-accessible surface areas and fewer protein-water hydrogen bonds in D2O coexist with longer water residence times at specific structural sites. In CI-2, the strongest changes localize to the second {beta}-strand/C-terminal region; in Bn-B*, persistent hydration is concentrated at the charged protein-protein interface. Together, these results support a model in which D2O dependent stabilization is associated not only with the extent of hydration, but the site and lifetime of water interactions. More broadly, this work provides an experimental framework for resolving solvent-dependent conformational thermodynamics of protein unfolding and interactions, enabling direct comparison of free-energy landscapes across solution environments.

title: Closing the phenotyping gap: non-invasive electromagnetic induction enables high-throughput screening of crop root function in the field
summary: Crop root systems play a critical role in water uptake and yield improvement under drought. However, a lack of methods to measure root system function at scale, particularly in the field, poses significant challenges to explore them in crop improvement programs. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a novel approach to directly screen water uptake and root activity in the field through integrating electromagnetic induction (EMI) sensing, inversion modelling and machine learning. This study was conducted as an on-farm field experiment comprising a factorial combination of 13 sorghum genotypes and three row spacings with three replications. Time-lapse EMI surveys were conducted from flowering to maturity using a customised DualEM-21S sensing system. Artificial neural network models were developed to predict 3D soil moisture ({theta}) using depth-specific true soil electrical conductivity estimated from EMI inversion algorithms, and the prediction accuracy was evaluated. Crop water use and functional root traits were derived from changes in {theta} profiles between successive EMI surveys using cubic splines fitted within a linear mixed model framework. Results indicate that dynamics of {theta} can be predicted with high accuracy (R2 = 0.83). There was a significant positive correlation between the EMI-derived crop water use and root length density at the depths without water stress. The functional root traits were significantly affected by growth stages, genotypes, row spacings, and their interactions. In general, narrower row spacing resulted in deeper rooting depth by flowering, which was associated with a larger canopy and higher grain number. In contrast, wider row spacing promoted greater post-flowering root growth, leading to increased post-flowering water use and, consequently, larger grain weight. Overall, our approach enables rapid characterisation of variation in crop water use, rooting depth and root growth in the field. It provides a valuable framework for understanding the dynamic interactions between root function and yield traits across variable field environments, with potential to accelerate genotype selection and optimise crop design in breeding and agronomy programs.

title: Discrete-time quantum walks reveal critical residues involved in long-range interactions in proteins
summary: Abstract: Long-range interactions between residues in proteins underlie diverse biological processes such as signal transmission, conformational regulation, and catalysis. Identifying residues that mediate such communication remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce a framework based on quantum walks and entropy, and employ it on protein structures to predict important residues participating in long-range interactions. The selected proteins have been well-studied experimentally in literature. Our approach models information flow through protein contact networks using discrete-time quantum walk dynamics, where quantum superposition and interference govern transition amplitudes at the residue level. Normalized time-averaged transition probabilities quantify interaction strength between residues, while Shannon entropy calculations identify residues exhibiting delocalized interaction behavior. We find that the residues identified by us are known to be structurally and functionally important in literature. We experimentally validate our formalism on AsLOV2 (PDB: 2V0U) using site-directed mutagenesis, protein purification, and dark-recovery kinetics. The predicted residues are important for understanding the mechanism of photosensing in AsLOV2. Significance: This study bridges quantum transport theory and structural biology by introducing discrete-time quantum walks as a mechanism to model communication between residues. We provide a scalable and interpretable method to predict key residues, without requiring molecular dynamics or prior functional annotation. The present method, inspired by quantum physics and quantum information, and validated by experiments, offers a broad and robust framework to study communication in biomolecular systems. It further demonstrates how quantum principles such as coherence and interference can enhance our understanding of information flow in biological macromolecules.

title: Predicting conformational changes induced by biomolecular interactions
summary: Biomolecular interactions trigger structural changes of protein complexes essential for cellular signaling, regulation, and drug action. Modern co-folding models can now generate detailed structures of multi-component complexes directly from sequence. However, recent evaluations reveal that they frequently fail to capture specific conformational states induced by a ligand or partner. Here, we show that explicitly modeling the structural transition from an unbound to a bound state, rather than generating the bound complex alone, better resolves these interaction-induced states. Our generative learning framework, K-Fold, transforms independently predicted unbound component priors into an assembled complex through an ultrafast diffusion bridge, operating entirely without multiple sequence alignments. By eliminating co-evolutionary dependencies, K-Fold accurately recovers non-coevolved interfaces in antibody-antigen and targeted-degrader complexes, as well as ligand-directed regulatory states in GPCRs and kinases. Furthermore, by coupling this diffusion bridge with diverse monomeric equilibrium ensembles, K-Fold provides a computationally tractable foundation for sampling complex multi-state landscapes without retraining. These results demonstrate that formulating molecular assembly as an explicit structural transition moves structure prediction beyond static geometries toward capturing biomolecular dynamics.

title: Computational alternative to cardiac biopsy in multiple myeloma: utilizing the shape of routine laboratory data for the classification of AL cardiac amyloidosis
summary: Background: Patients with multiple myeloma (MM) are at increased risk for light chain cardiac amyloidosis (CA) due to high circulating levels of light chains. ALCA is a clinical diagnosis based on biopsy, cardiac imaging findings of restrictive cardiomyopathy, and serum monoclonal proteins. To overcome these challenges, we have developed machine learning models that accurately predict ALCA status while identifying key diagnostic features based on routine laboratory measurements and using limited data. Methods: Utilizing electronic medical data (EMR) data, we built support vector machine models (SVMs) using the MISTIC framework. Data including diagnosis history, treatment, and laboratory values for patients with MM or monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance (MGUS) were collected as a retrospective cohort study at Moffit Cancer Center and Research Institute between 2014 and 2019. To utilize the wealth of information in longitudinal EMR data, we fit regression models to the EMR data and used the parameters and characteristics of the fits as features for our SVMs. We tested three different sets of features: descriptive statistics alone, parameters and characteristics of fit only, and both the descriptive statistics and parameters of fit (DescFits). A classifier using raw data at a timepoint proximal to the date of ALCA diagnostic imaging (EchoAdj), as well as analogous random forest and XGBoost models were used for comparison. Findings: SVM classifiers trained on the DescFits feature set (AUC= 1.0) outperformed blind model predictions of the EchoAdj model (AUC = 0.36) and other conventional machine learning approaches in identifying which patients were diagnosed with ALCA. The DescFits model selected features describing the temporal relationship of physiologic parameters including hematologic state, and cardiac and renal function. Interpretation: We demonstrated that the MISTIC SVM framework and the shape of EMR data can aid in identifying patients with cardiac amyloidosis without cardiac biopsy or imaging.

title: Binning-based Methods for Model Fitting and Data Splitting Improve Machine Learning Imbalanced Regression
summary: Modelling quantitative genomics data remains challenging due to imbalanced target distributions, non-independent observations, and substantial computational costs. This study examines the challenges and current methods, proposes new methods, applies these methods across two case studies: a controlled setting with synthetically generated data and on real genomics datasets. Effective modelling of imbalanced data starts with density estimation. Density estimation via binning facilitates downstream analytical steps. Minimum Transformation Binning is a novel method that improves current binning methods for density estimation. Data splitting of imbalanced and non-independent observations is best accomplished by objective data splitting which entails randomly generating splits, scoring them, and selecting the best scoring one. This study conducts an empirical comparison of scoring functions toward an optimal objective data splitting method, finding the use of all-against-one absolute relative difference to be the best scoring function. Model fitting methods can be divided into loss functions and data balancing. Two methods have been previously proposed based on weighting error functions by the reciprocal or complement of the density estimation. This study conducts a comparison of these methods on the case studies, finding that reciprocal density weighting significantly outperforms non-weighted and complement density weighting. This study also tests model fitting with reciprocal weighted sampling per epoch for imbalanced regression. While this method does not generally improve performance, it uses significantly less resources in model fitting which can be beneficial for hyperparameter optimization. Together, this study provides a unified framework for effective modelling of imbalanced regression, especially imbalanced genomics data.
